input.command:
cat > diagnosis.json <<'EOF'
{"spec_element": "requires",
 "proof_obligation": "initiation",
 "diagnosis": "The precondition of predicate 'sorted' is 'n <= a.Length + 1', which is off by one: it admits n == a.Length + 1, in which case the quantifier ranges over j == a.Length and a[j] is out of bounds (counterexample a.Length = 7720, n = 7721). The well-formedness of the predicate body is not established by its requires clause. Fix: require n <= a.Length."}
EOF
sed -i '3s/requires n <= (a.Length) + 1/requires n <= a.Length/' program.dfy && sed -n 3p program.dfy && dafny verify program.dfy

content.content:
requires n <= a.Length

Dafny program verifier finished with 4 verified, 0 errors

content.text:
Fixed: Dafny now verifies `program.dfy` (4 verified, 0 errors).

**What was wrong:** the `sorted` predicate's `requires` clause (line 3) was off by one. It said `n <= (a.Length) + 1`, which allows `n == a.Length + 1`. In that case the body's `forall i,j :: 0 <= i < j < n ==> a[i] <= a[j]` can pick `j == a.Length`, so `a[j]` is out of bounds. That matches the counterexample (`a.Length = 7720`, `n = 7721`). The precondition didn't guarantee the predicate body was well-formed.

**Fix:** I changed the precondition to `requires n <= a.Length`. Every call in the file uses `sorted(a, a.Length)`, so the stricter precondition still holds at each call.

I wrote `diagnosis.json` before the edit, classifying this as `requires` / `initiation`. "Initiation" is the closest of the three given categories, since the problem is the precondition failing to set up what the body needs. Strictly speaking, though, there's no loop involved here; it's a well-formedness failure in the predicate's precondition.
